Yes, under the current affairs they had of course been requesting, they were undertaking, you know, what I would call economic measures, where they concluded on page 1D 57-0655 that a particular request from the match factory, factory producing matches, had been granted, and of course saying that they would have to do under particular condition a typical measure that would usually not be undertaken by a local community but here they were, of course -- this is the war situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You need to slow down a little bit, and then I want to make sure that the record is very clear. The numbers that you are referring to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I want to be very clear for the record. The numbers that you have been referring to are at the bottom right-hand corner, and the last part that you spoke of is under item 8, I guess, current affairs, or paragraph 8, number 8. And you were referring to that section; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: That is correct. Since the document is not paged, I used the bottom right...

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go on to the next document, 1D 0 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Witness, we've just seen a document which is interesting because it does not stem from the HVO but from a municipality controlled by Muslims. utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I have -- when I was looking into all these documents, especially the documents from Tuzla for which I knew that it is Muslim controlled, I was for the first time surprised that the measures are very similar. So when I over the weekend received these documents from Travnik confirming, you know, again, that in the central Bosnia, you know, the same situation and also later on we've seen some of the same in Jablanica, that is just reiterate my conclusion which I made as discussing issues and looking into documents for the local communities that the measures were done in an equal manner notwithstanding whether it was a Muslim majority or Croat majority area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go on to the next document, which is 1D 02977, staying, again, with Travnik, if you could please give us an opinion on this document.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Yes. Here I would like to refer -- there is a meeting of the executive committee of this municipality of Travnik. The agenda has been set. This is December 20, 1993, and I would like to refer to two issues on the agenda: Number 5, deliberation on the programme of measures for a more efficient collection of taxes; and number 8, current affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. So let's go by page so we can locate them.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I would like now first to refer to page 4. This copy has been paged. And under page -- in page 4, there is a section 85, and in the middle there are conclusions saying that the programme of measures for a more efficient collection of taxes is hereby adopted together with the commanded conclusions, and point 2, the Executive Committee hereby tasks the municipal administration of income to prepare a write-off of fixtures due, which means writing-off of the state obligations, and that is, you know, something that they had been asked by the decree on law about the role of the socio-economic -- socio-political communities. But I would like also to draw attention to page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Before we go to page 5, sticking with page 2, again, we need to make a very clear record, and you indicated that they were asked to write off dues, and then you made reference. Is that to the law that we saw earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: That is the law which we saw earlier. That is the decree law on the application of the law on the financing of general social needs, document 1D 02047.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So this is an example of a particular municipality acting upon the new authority that it has been granted. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, what's the next part?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: The next part is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers kindly not overlap for the interpreters. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This was well overdue, this admonishment. So ...

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to raise your attention to page 5 of the document 1D 02977, and on page 5, in the bottom of that page, there are conclusions on so-called (b), processing of bills. There seems to be an activity of creating money at the level of Travnik municipality for the due pensions, and I would also like to refer --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Wait. Hold on, because we want to make sure we're clear because we're not economists. What do you mean that they're creating money?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Well, obviously, they had some physical Bosnian dinars.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: And this seems to overstem them so that they be worth more so that they would be able to pay the pensions out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, whose function is that?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Well, that is normally the function of the central bank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Sorry. I also stumbled at the word "process," to process BH bills, and I wondered whether process here means printed, but it's printing, but it seems that you say they took a stamp and they took whatever bill because it is not said here, and then stamp 100, and make 28.000 of those. Do you have an idea what practically happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah. From my understanding is this is -- this is what usually happened in the high inflation time. You are renominating the bills in order, you know, to have a higher value. And that's why it is not surprise, and I would like, Your Honours, to draw your attention to page 6 on the top of that -- page 6 on the top. There is a statement issued by the executive committee says: "The executive committee once again warns the postal and telephone services, the utilities company, the heating company and electric company of Travnik when collecting their dues to accept Bosnian-Herzegovinian dinar bills." You have a local community enterprises that were not trusting Bosnia-Herzegovina dinar bills, so the executive committee had to request them to collect legal tender. So there was such a low lack of trust that even the electrical company in Travnik would not accept BH dinar bills. And of course, this is middle of 1993 with a very high inflation, and that's why I say that this is just a description how difficult situation was and why really the national bank of Bosnia-Herzegovina was not controlling the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. It seems that translation is perhaps not the happiest one. What you interpret this to mean is that the postal and telephone service are told not to accept BHD bills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They are warned -- it once again warns them to accept. They were not accepting them. And so the executive committee warns the postal and telephone services that when collecting their dues, to accept BH dinar bills.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Just, I guess, one point of clarification that was, I guess, prompted from one of the questions from Judge Trechsel when you indicated that usually the money is renominated with the stamp. Let's say that you take this newly nominated currency to another municipality. Do you know what, if any, value that currency would have? Would it have the value that Travnik municipality places on it or Sarajevo or what?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Well, most likely it would not have that value because people would only take the face value. But if there's a stamp over the Travnik municipality that this is now not 1.000 but 10.000 dinars, people in Tuzla might not accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment. There may be a problem with the translation because when you say "bill" in English, well, in French it was interpreted as "facture," so bill, but I have my doubts. Is this not money, paper money, because if a bill is in BH dinars, how by which miraculous operation could the bill be transformed as to the amounts? So are we talking about bank notes that have a higher nominal value, are given a higher nominal value? Are we talking about bills issued by any order, enterprise or company?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if I'm -- you know, I'm a central banker, so American term would be US dollar bill. European term would be US dollar bank note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not to be confused with bill as in receipt?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Exactly. And that's why I believe this translation talks about the bank notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go to on the next document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So you can see that I was ever so right in stepping in. So bill here is a bank note?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Exactly. Exactly. And I read Croatian, and here they talk about -- sorry, B/C/S, Croatia, Bosnian, Serbian. Here they talk about "novcanica," and "novcanica" is a bank note.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If we go on to the next document, 1D 02980. I would like to finish the next four documents very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: This is the decision of the municipality of Tuzla to establish duty-free shops that would help them to get some more goods into the territory, and that is defined in Article Roman i and Roman ii and Roman iii of that document 1D 02980.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And again, is this a function that normally would be undertaken by a municipality or by the state itself?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: That would be functions taken by the ministry of finance of a state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look at 1D 00244, staying with Tuzla municipality.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: That is an order issued on December 1992 by presidency of the Tuzla municipality assembly to issue an order on obligatory payment of war tax in foreign currency. Local community of Tuzla did not trust Bosnia-Herzegovina dinars. They were already issued by that time, I believe, and here they ask that, in Article 1st, all legal entities and natural persons involved in foreign trade are hereby obliged to pay a sum of money in foreign currency. They defined that sum of money as war tax, and it should be paid as 20 percent of that special tax if they would instead of paying money -- paying tax -- instead of paying tax in foreign currency, and they would instead of foreign currency giving goods, giving things in kind, then the tax would be 15 percent as stated in the third paragraph of Article 1st of that varied order.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And then we can see in Article 2 where there are some exemptions.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Well, yes. There is in Article 2 exemptions. If they import goods in order to hand it over to directorate of rationing because they establish -- I understand they had a special directorate where they were delivering goods to the society, then there is no tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And again, with respect to the -- to the Article 1, the activities that you just described, are those normally state activities, or is the municipality entitled to do -- to undertake these sorts of measures?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: These are normally state authority. However, they've done this given the war circumstances by local authority themselves. And I have discussed this very issue with the Presidency, asking why he did that, because that looks like, you know, he was stimulating the so-called war profiteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Who did you discuss this with?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: I discussed this with Mr. Beslagic during my visit to Bosnia-Herzegovina in December 20th, 2007. I met him and ask him --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What position did he have at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: He was -- Mr. Beslagic was the one who actually issued that order in December of 1992, so ask him during my visit why such an order, and he had explained that in order to get goods into the country, into the local community of Tuzla, he had also stimulate -- you know, he stimulate the activities of the traders, and he took for the benefit of the community the 20 percent as special tax.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we go on to the next document. 1D 03021.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: This is the decision by the Croatian Defence Council of Grude of August 10, 1993, defining in Article 2 that the material obligation for citizens of the municipality of Grude working abroad shall be set -- and that is for those that they have the permanent Visas, shall be set at 200 Deutschemark for men and 100 Deutschemark for women, which means that they impose a fiscal obligation on the citizens to finance the needs of the council of the Grude municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And finally, the last document for this slide is 1D 03019, and I believe this is Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Yes, this is Zenica. This was new document for me. It is a decision of September 30, 1993, on provision of funds for procurement of material and technical needs for the needs of armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it says in Article 4 that privately -- obligations of the privately owned company shall be defined depending on the type of business activity, if it is registered for, that forms the majority part of its activity, and it says that the wholesale shop should pay from 1.000 to 4.000 Deutschemark of a special tax for covering the needs of that varying municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Why is that important?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Well, that is important because they have actually undertaken measures to collect funds from local private businesses in order, of course, to finance the needs of Zenica municipality, again, a function of the state being undertaken by local community.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as I understand it, the documents that we saw which were just sort of, for lack of a better term, vignettes or examples, these are the sort of documents that you were looking at and relying on in forming the sorts of conclusions that we see on slide 27; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: That is correct. On slide 27, I explain in the bottom what kind of measures they were undertaking, and then of course on slide 28, if I --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're not going to go into 28 because we are going to be finishing. I just wanted to conclude with that that --

utterances.speaker: MILAN CVIKL
utterances.text: Yes. On slide 27 and the documents which we presented are the type of the measures to support defence, to undertake macroeconomic measures, which means control of the fiscal revenues, to undertake the role of the central bank and the microeconomic measures; that means the support of the enterprises sectors that would be normally the function of the state, and all that had been done by the local communities which have been here presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cvikl. Your Honours, I see the time. This is actually a perfect opportunity for us to break, as we go on to the next segment tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, you have used 2 hours and 17 minutes, for your information. Witness, you shall return tomorrow at 2.15, since we sit in the afternoons this week. Until then, you are of course not allowed to have any contact whatsoever, not with the press, either, in case you would like to comment anything about questions and answers. I wish you all a very good evening, and I look forward to seeing you tomorrow at 2.15.
